In the final frame (image 10), the part reaches the far right edge of the ramp structure and appears to be tilted/falling off the track entirely, overhanging the edge where it would land. This behavior—traversing the trap but then failing to continue or falling off—is consistent with post-trap rejection, defined as the part being pushed off or amidst falling off the track on the right side after encountering the ramp. The object's unusual geometry may contribute to this specific trajectory over a simple roundplate.
